clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around Teodor's death in January 1978: within months, Delphine stopped cooking and went to her daughter Odette's every evening; Duncan took night shifts and distanced from Odette; Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work; Odette's anxiety over her mother and Anton rose; and Callum developed ear infections through the winter. Hazel's quarrel with Simone over the house is undated and left out. By May 1979, Delphine took a job at the library and her functioning rose, settling the period.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest in pregnancy, 1984
clusters.reason: Around Odette ordered to bed in March 1984: within months, Hazel came every morning to keep the house; Duncan argued with his mother over how she kept it; Callum stammered again after a year free of it; and by September, Ines was born. Your own anxiety about your father sitting by your bed is undated and left out. The shifts around Hazel's overfunctioning and Duncan's conflict with her, alongside Callum's return of symptoms, show the family's reactions in those months.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around Hazel's diagnosis of Parkinson's in September 1986: over the following decade, Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; Duncan phoned his father every night for news; Hazel fell in the kitchen and walked with a frame; Duncan and Lyle argued over who should help their parents; Ambrose developed chest pains; Hazel needed dressing; Odette took her to the clinic twice a week; Mavis came to nurse her one week in four; Duncan drank most evenings; Pearl had panic spells at the wheel; and Ambrose gave up his workshop and hardly left Hazel's side. A good summer in 1994 brought temporary relief. By June 1997, when Hazel moved to the nursing home, the intensity of the family's reactions eased.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around Callum leaving home in May 1999 for a job up north: in the months before and after, Duncan and Callum argued most nights; Odette could not settle at the thought of him so far away; Duncan missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; Ines skipped school through the autumn; Odette took Ines with her everywhere; and by August 2000, Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams. The shifts show the family pulled in different directions as Callum went, each one's move tied to the next.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around Hazel's death in January 2003: within months, you could not sleep more than a few hours; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; by November, you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.

An acute episode around a real event, settled within a few days.
